# Lifecycle table
{: .no_toc }

This is the contribution state machine as defined in `lifecycle.py`: 27 states, 228 transitions with 93 distinct verbs (65 of the transitions are expanded from 5 rules), 1 flag, and 13 retry budgets, plus the operation table with 6 states and 14 transitions. A contribution starts in `queued.idle` (`accept_request`).

A requested task is identified by its generation, revision, and task id. A Result that differs in any of them is never folded and never published.

## Triggers

| Trigger | Meaning |
|:--------|:--------|
| `command` | An authorized `/upstreaming` command. Commands that activate or approve work name the exact current revision; stop commands may name a stale one. |
| `observation` | A read-only observation by the collector: fork branch, CI runs, pull requests, review comments, or releases. |
| `result` | A verified native-queue Result folded by reconciliation. A Result is folded only when it matches the current generation, revision, and a requested task; any other Result takes `record_late_effect`. Each Result records its token usage in the events. |
| `operation` | A trusted remote operation receipt and its exact readback. |
| `tick` | A controller decision without new input: task allocation, a budget charge or exhaustion, a deadline, or the stop after an unexpected error while one contribution was processed. |

## State kinds

| Kind | Meaning |
|:-----|:--------|
| `auto_wait` | Waits for an automatic trigger; the controller acts without a human. A guard that does not hold yet (a worker slot, capacity) keeps the contribution here; there is no separate capacity wait. |
| `running` | A requested task or a trusted operation is in progress. |
| `human_wait` | A recorded `pending_human_action` names what a human must do; `/upstreaming resume` continues. |
| `gate` | Waits for a human command that starts the next step. |
| `locked` | Write-fenced wait: only the listed exits leave it, and no task, patch, or branch write happens while here. |
| `generation_end` | The current generation has ended; the record is kept for audit and late-effect reconciliation until a clean restart with `/upstreaming refresh`. |
| `terminal` | No transition leaves this state. |

## States

*Launches* means the controller may allocate a task or launch remote effects from the state, subject to the flags. *Fork writes* means automated writers may write the contribution fork. *Exits* counts the state's own transitions and, after the plus sign, the rule transitions that apply in it.

| State | Kind | Launches | Fork writes | Exits | Description |
|:------|:-----|:---------|:------------|:------|:------------|
| `queued.idle` | `auto_wait` | yes | no | 6 + 3 | An accepted request is recorded; planning has not started. |
| `planning.idle` | `auto_wait` | yes | no | 7 + 3 | Planning is due; the controller allocates a planning task when a worker slot is free. |
| `planning.agent_running` | `running` | no | no | 10 + 2 | A planning task is requested or running and will return a plan. |
| `planning.waiting_human` | `human_wait` | no | no | 4 + 3 | Planning recovery or a budget is exhausted; a human corrects the cause and resumes. |
| `provisioning.idle` | `running` | yes | yes | 7 + 4 | The fork provisioning operation is planned or running through the trusted workflow. |
| `provisioning.waiting_human` | `human_wait` | no | no | 3 + 4 | Provisioning cannot continue safely; a human corrects the prerequisite and resumes, or parks. While the planned operation of exhausted launches is open, `park` and a resume after `refresh.stale_after_days` days first need it closed with `/upstreaming resolve-operation`. |
| `development.agent_running` | `running` | no | yes | 12 + 3 | A patch task is requested or running, or its Result is being verified. The worker implements the patch, reviews it in its own run with a review loop on the `subagent` tool of `pi-subagents` (at most 3 rounds of fresh reviewers), and publishes it there; a Result whose loop ended with a P0 finding open is rejected and publishes nothing. |
| `development.waiting_ci` | `auto_wait` | no | yes | 14 + 3 | A patch is published to the development PR; CI and review evaluate the exact head. Passing CI nominates the head, or returns to `development.fix_needed` while actionable feedback is pending or a series requirement of the plan is unmet; passing CI behind an open operation keeps the contribution here. The controller opens the development PR of the published head through a trusted operation. |
| `development.fix_needed` | `auto_wait` | yes | yes | 15 + 4 | A development task is due: the fork is ready for a first patch, or a CI failure, actionable review, passing CI with feedback still pending, rejected proposal, refreshed plan, or a resume needs a bounded repair. It is the only state in which a patch task is requested, so none is requested before `confirm_provisioning`. |
| `development.waiting_human` | `human_wait` | no | no | 6 + 4 | Development recovery, or the recovery of a publication, or `task_total` is exhausted, the development PR does not match, CI on the head was interrupted repeatedly, or the development PR operation could not be completed; a human corrects the cause and resumes. |
| `handoff.awaiting_submission` | `gate` | no | no | 6 + 3 | Required CI passed on the exact head; a human may request upstream submission. |
| `handoff.review_due` | `auto_wait` | yes | no | 6 + 3 | The submission rewrite is due; the controller allocates a rewrite task when a worker slot is free. |
| `handoff.agent_running` | `running` | no | no | 6 + 2 | A submission rewrite task is requested or running; its Result is the rewritten series, title, and description, or the reasons the series cannot be shaped without a code change. |
| `handoff.building_upstream_branch` | `running` | no | yes | 6 + 2 | The upstream branch `riscv64` is created, or replaced under an exact-head lease, from the reviewed series, and read back. It is never written while an upstream PR is open from it, and `riscv64-dev` is not changed. |
| `handoff.waiting_ci` | `auto_wait` | no | no | 5 + 2 | Required CI runs on the clean head of `riscv64`. |
| `handoff.preparing_submission` | `running` | no | no | 4 + 2 | The submission package (title, body, prefilled compare link) is posted to the tracking issue. It is posted only while `riscv64` still resolves to the clean head. |
| `handoff.waiting_human` | `human_wait` | no | no | 7 + 3 | A handoff step failed repeatedly or needs a human: the submission rewrite task, writing `riscv64` (also while an upstream PR is open from it), CI on the clean head, or posting the submission package. A human corrects it and resumes; the resume returns to the step named by `pending_human_action` and starts again the counter named in `pending_human_action.counter`. |
| `handoff.waiting_upstream_pr` | `locked` | no | no | 4 + 2 | Waiting for a human to open the upstream PR from the package. Exactly three exits leave it: `verify_upstream_pr`, `retract_submission`, and `refresh_planning`. |
| `upstream_review.waiting_ci` | `auto_wait` | no | no | 7 + 1 | The upstream PR is open; upstream CI, review, and merge are observed. Upstream CI is never rerun by the pipeline. |
| `upstream_review.fix_needed` | `auto_wait` | yes | yes | 8 + 2 | Upstream CI or actionable review needs a revision of the upstream PR head. |
| `upstream_review.agent_running` | `running` | no | yes | 8 + 1 | A revision task for the upstream PR head is requested or running, or its verified Result is being published. |
| `upstream_review.waiting_human` | `human_wait` | no | no | 6 + 3 | The upstream PR was closed unmerged, its head changed, a reviewer needs an answer, or recovery or a budget is exhausted; a human triages. |
| `release_wait.idle` | `auto_wait` | no | no | 3 + 1 | The upstream PR is merged; the official release is observed: PyPI coverage of a recorded target contract, else the first PyPI release of the distributions or the first GitHub release of the upstream repository after the merge that has a linux riscv64 wheel or asset. |
| `release_wait.waiting_human` | `human_wait` | no | no | 1 + 2 | Release evidence needs operator action. |
| `released.idle` | `terminal` | no | no | 0 + 1 | Verified official release coverage satisfies the acceptance contract. |
| `parked.idle` | `generation_end` | no | no | 2 + 1 | The generation ended without success; a clean restart is possible. |
| `closed.idle` | `terminal` | no | no | 0 + 1 | No further work: withdrawn, not applicable, already satisfied, or abandoned. The reason is `terminal_reason`. |

## State invariants

Every record in a state satisfies the invariants the state requires. `lifecycle check` proves that no row enters a state without them: each requirement of the target is kept from the source, implied by a guard of the row, established by its effects, or (`not_paused`) assured by the mask of the flag. The engine refuses a row from a record that breaks its state (`source_invalid`), but for the stops, a late Result and the row that heals the invariant, and a row whose record after it breaks its target (`target_invalid`).

| Invariant | Meaning | Implied by | Healed by |
|:----------|:--------|:-----------|:----------|
| `bound` | the upstream identity and base are bound | upstream identity and base bound | the stop after a processing error |
| `plan` | a verified plan and its admitted scope are recorded | - | the stop after a processing error |
| `fork` | the fork is recorded | refresh recorded | the stop after a processing error |
| `dev_pr` | a development PR and its head are recorded | development PR and head recorded | `launch_development_pr`, `confirm_development_pr`, `record_pr_mismatch` |
| `task` | A task is requested | - | the stop after a processing error |
| `task_or_publication` | A task is requested, or the publication of its Result is held | - | the stop after a processing error |
| `pending` | a pending human action is recorded | - | the stop after a processing error |
| `no_pending` | no pending human action is recorded | - | the stop after a processing error |
| `candidate` | the candidate head of the submission is the recorded fork head | - | the stop after a processing error |
| `upstream_pr` | the upstream PR is recorded | - | the stop after a processing error |
| `merge` | the merge of the upstream PR is recorded | - | the stop after a processing error |
| `parked_reason` | the reason of the park is recorded | - | the stop after a processing error |
| `not_paused` | the contribution is not paused | not paused | the stop after a processing error |

| State | Requires |
|:------|:---------|
| `queued.idle` | `no_pending` |
| `planning.idle` | `no_pending` |
| `planning.agent_running` | `bound`, `task`, `no_pending`, `not_paused` |
| `planning.waiting_human` | `pending` |
| `provisioning.idle` | `plan`, `no_pending` |
| `provisioning.waiting_human` | `plan`, `pending` |
| `development.agent_running` | `bound`, `plan`, `fork`, `task_or_publication`, `no_pending`, `not_paused` |
| `development.waiting_ci` | `bound`, `plan`, `fork`, `dev_pr`, `no_pending` |
| `development.fix_needed` | `bound`, `plan`, `fork`, `no_pending` |
| `development.waiting_human` | `bound`, `plan`, `fork`, `pending` |
| `handoff.awaiting_submission` | `bound`, `plan`, `fork`, `dev_pr`, `candidate`, `pending` |
| `handoff.review_due` | `bound`, `plan`, `fork`, `dev_pr`, `no_pending` |
| `handoff.agent_running` | `bound`, `plan`, `fork`, `dev_pr`, `task`, `no_pending`, `not_paused` |
| `handoff.building_upstream_branch` | `bound`, `plan`, `fork`, `dev_pr`, `no_pending` |

| `handoff.preparing_submission` | `bound`, `plan`, `fork`, `dev_pr`, `no_pending` |

| `upstream_review.waiting_ci` | `bound`, `plan`, `fork`, `upstream_pr`, `no_pending` |

An effect normally clears a whole field. These entries clear a part of one.

| Entry | Field | What is cleared |
|:------|:------|:----------------|
| `carried pending_feedback_evidence_ids` | `pending_feedback_evidence_ids` | exactly the ids in `active_task.feedback_evidence_ids`, the pending feedback present when the task was allocated; feedback recorded later stays pending |

## Rules

A rule is a transition that applies in many states. It is written once and expanded into one row per state; the rows appear under each state below, marked *(rule)*.

### `park_contribution`
{: #rule-park_contribution }

Applies in every non-terminal state except `parked.idle`, `handoff.waiting_upstream_pr`, `release_wait.*`, and `upstream_review.*` other than `upstream_review.waiting_human`.

| Verb | Trigger | To | Guard | Effects | Charges |
|:-----|:--------|:---|:------|:--------|:--------|
| `park_contribution` | command (`/upstreaming park`) | `parked.idle` | a reason is given; any revision, current or stale; no open operation. Ends the current generation; evidence is kept for audit. A Result held for publication is not published. Accepted while paused. | Task: clear; sets `parked_reason`, `previous_phase`; clears `pending_publication` | - |

Expanded into: `queued.idle`, `planning.idle`, `planning.agent_running`, `planning.waiting_human`, `provisioning.idle`, `provisioning.waiting_human`, `development.agent_running`, `development.waiting_ci`, `development.fix_needed`, `development.waiting_human`, `handoff.awaiting_submission`, `handoff.review_due`, `handoff.agent_running`, `handoff.building_upstream_branch`, `handoff.waiting_ci`, `handoff.preparing_submission`, `handoff.waiting_human`, `upstream_review.waiting_human`.

### `resume_stale`
{: #rule-resume_stale }

Applies in every `provisioning.*` and `development.*` state.

| Verb | Trigger | To | Guard | Effects | Charges |
|:-----|:--------|:---|:------|:--------|:--------|
| `resume_stale` | command (`/upstreaming resume`) | `queued.idle` | exact revision; paused, or waiting for a human; stopped for longer than `refresh.stale_after_days` days; quiescent: no open operation and no pending publication; no requested task. After a long stop the plan is refreshed: complete planning runs again while the fork and development PR are kept. The stop is counted from the older of `paused_at` and `pending_human_action.requested_at`. While an operation is open no resume applies, and the rejection names the open operation. From a human wait that an exhausted budget caused, it starts again the counter named in `pending_human_action.counter`, like every resume. | revision +1; sets `refresh`; clears `plan_evidence_id`, `scope_coverage_complete`, `scope_paths`, `proposal_artifact`, `last_ci_evidence_id`, `clean_head_sha`, `handoff_request`, `handoff_approval`, `pending_human_action`, `publication_operation_id`, `pending_publication`, `paused`, `paused_at`, `paused_reason`, `paused_by`, `paused_at_commit`; starts again the counter named in `pending_human_action.counter` (one of `operation_launch`, `interrupted_reruns`, `dispatch_recovery`, `task_recovery`, `task_total`, `publish_recovery`, `source_reads`) | - |

Expanded into: `provisioning.idle`, `provisioning.waiting_human`, `development.agent_running`, `development.waiting_ci`, `development.fix_needed`, `development.waiting_human`.

### `record_reminder`
{: #rule-record_reminder }

Applies in every state of kind `gate`, `human_wait`, or `locked`.

| Verb | Trigger | To | Guard | Effects | Charges |
|:-----|:--------|:---|:------|:--------|:--------|
| `record_reminder` | tick | same state | at least `human_sla_business_days.reminder` business days since the request or the last reminder; not paused. Posts an append-only reminder of the pending human step. In `handoff.waiting_upstream_pr` the reminder text carries the package link and the exact head, and states when an observed PR does not match. Days are whole days from the exact time of the request or of the last reminder; a day counts when it ends on a weekday (UTC). A reminder that came due during a pause is posted after the resume, in the same tick. | sets `pending_human_action.reminded_at` | - |

Expanded into: `planning.waiting_human`, `provisioning.waiting_human`, `development.waiting_human`, `handoff.awaiting_submission`, `handoff.waiting_human`, `handoff.waiting_upstream_pr`, `upstream_review.waiting_human`, `release_wait.waiting_human`.

### `record_source_unavailable`
{: #rule-record_source_unavailable }

Applies in every state in which the controller needs the upstream base branch: `queued.idle`, `planning.idle`, `provisioning.idle`, `development.fix_needed`, `handoff.review_due` and `upstream_review.fix_needed`.

| Verb | Trigger | To | Guard | Effects | Charges |
|:-----|:--------|:---|:------|:--------|:--------|
| `record_source_unavailable` | observation | same state | the upstream repository or its base branch could not be read, and the upstream did not say that the branch is missing; source_reads remains; not paused; quiescent: no open operation and no pending publication. A network error, a server error, a rate limit, or a repository that cannot be read: the contribution stays, and a later tick reads the upstream again. A failed read is charged only when it is the first of a run, or when it falls in a later spacing slot than the last charged read (slots of `retries.source_unavailable_minutes` divided by `retries.source_unavailable_reads`, counted from the first failed read, so that a tick a little early or late still counts); a failed read in the same slot writes nothing, so a burst of ticks adds no events, and a read after a long pause counts once. A tick that reads the upstream starts `source_reads` again. | none | `source_reads` |

Expanded into: `queued.idle`, `planning.idle`, `provisioning.idle`, `development.fix_needed`, `handoff.review_due`, `upstream_review.fix_needed`.

### `record_late_effect`
{: #rule-record_late_effect }

Applies in every state.

| Verb | Trigger | To | Guard | Effects | Charges |
|:-----|:--------|:---|:------|:--------|:--------|
| `record_late_effect` | result | same state | the Result does not match the current generation, revision, and a requested task. Recorded in the events for audit. The Result is never folded, the publisher refuses it, and the state never changes. | none | - |

Expanded into: `queued.idle`, `planning.idle`, `planning.agent_running`, `planning.waiting_human`, `provisioning.idle`, `provisioning.waiting_human`, `development.agent_running`, `development.waiting_ci`, `development.fix_needed`, `development.waiting_human`, `handoff.awaiting_submission`, `handoff.review_due`, `handoff.agent_running`, `handoff.building_upstream_branch`, `handoff.waiting_ci`, `handoff.preparing_submission`, `handoff.waiting_human`, `handoff.waiting_upstream_pr`, `upstream_review.waiting_ci`, `upstream_review.fix_needed`, `upstream_review.agent_running`, `upstream_review.waiting_human`, `release_wait.idle`, `release_wait.waiting_human`, `released.idle`, `parked.idle`, `closed.idle`.

## Flags

A flag is stored beside the state. It is set and cleared from every non-terminal state and keeps phase and activity, except where noted.

### `paused`
{: #flag-paused }

Stored in `paused`. A stop of a new task and writer admission, with its reason and who set it (a human or the controller) in `paused_reason` and `paused_by`. `pause` accepts an optional reason; a pause set by the controller always records one: `pause_on_identity_change` names it in the table, and `pause_on_processing_error` records the error. Setting it clears the requested task and the pending publication, and records `paused_at`; nothing held is published after the stop, and no publish retry is launched while paused. Phase, activity, evidence, and pending feedback are kept. The one exception: setting it in an `agent_running` state leads to the state in which the task is due again, `planning.idle`, `development.fix_needed`, `handoff.review_due`, or `upstream_review.fix_needed`; In `handoff.awaiting_submission` and `handoff.waiting_upstream_pr`, `resume_pause` keeps the plan, candidate head, clean head, `handoff_request`, and the posted package. `verify_upstream_pr` binds to the exact head only, so the revision bump does not invalidate the posted package; `submit_upstream` and `retract_submission` also name the exact revision, so after the bump they name the new revision with the same head, as the tracking-issue entries offer them. A row that ends the contribution (`closed.idle`, `released.idle`) clears the flag.

| Verb | Sets or clears | Trigger | Guard | Effects |
|:-----|:---------------|:--------|:------|:--------|
| `pause` | sets | command (`/upstreaming pause`) | not paused, or paused by the controller; not terminal; any revision, current or stale. A reason is optional; when given it is recorded in `paused_reason`. A pause the controller set is taken over: the stop is then the human's (`paused_by` `human`), and the controller no longer resumes it after a change of the pipeline code. | Task: clear; sets `paused`, `paused_at`, `paused_reason`, `paused_by=human`; clears `pending_publication`, `paused_at_commit` |
| `pause_on_identity_change` | sets | observation | not paused; not terminal; the observed upstream repository identity differs from the recorded one. A contribution that is already paused is not paused again: the change sets nothing, so the flag keeps its reason and who set it; no task is selected while the identity differs, and the first tick after the resume takes this row. | Task: clear; sets `paused`, `paused_at`, `paused_reason=upstream_identity_changed`, `paused_by=controller`; clears `pending_publication` |
| `pause_on_processing_error` | sets | tick | not paused; not terminal; an unexpected error while the controller processed this contribution in the tick. Everything the tick staged for the contribution and every effect it requested for it are discarded first, so the stop is taken on the record as it was committed before the tick. `paused_reason` states the error class, the bounded and sanitized message, and the run id. The tick continues with the other contributions. A contribution that is already paused is not paused again. Commands posted for the contribution are left unconsumed for the tick. `paused_at_commit` records the version of the pipeline code that ran, so the controller resumes the stop once that code changed. | Task: clear; sets `paused`, `paused_at`, `paused_reason`, `paused_by=controller`, `paused_at_commit`; clears `pending_publication` |
| `resume_pause` | clears | command (`/upstreaming resume`) | paused; exact revision; stopped for at most `refresh.stale_after_days` days, or the phase is not provisioning or development. A Result that landed during the pause no longer matches and takes `record_late_effect`. In a human wait the resume clears the flag only: the reply states that the contribution still waits for a human and names the pending action, and a second resume leaves the wait. No row leaves an ended contribution paused; a record that is paused and ended all the same has the flag cleared by a resume and nothing else. | revision +1; clears `paused`, `paused_at`, `paused_reason`, `paused_by`, `paused_at_commit` |

Setting the flag clears the requested task, so these states are left for the state in which that task is due again:

| From | To |
|:-----|:---|
| `planning.agent_running` | `planning.idle` |
| `development.agent_running` | `development.fix_needed` |
| `handoff.agent_running` | `handoff.review_due` |
| `upstream_review.agent_running` | `upstream_review.fix_needed` |

While set:

| Trigger | Effect |
|:--------|:-------|
| `command` | `resume`, `park`, `refresh`, `retract-pr`, `abandon`, and `resolve-operation` apply; other commands are rejected. `resume` clears the flag first: it takes `resume_pause` or `resume_stale`. In a human wait a second `resume` then leaves the wait. |
| `observation` | An observation that keeps the state and the revision is folded and saved (an explanation, a review comment fence); one that would move the record to another state (but one that ends it), bump the revision, or charge a budget is refused and read again after the resume, which takes the next step from what was saved. |
| `result` | The requested task and the pending publication were cleared, so a Result takes `record_late_effect`; nothing is published. |
| `operation` | Folded normally: a receipt finishes the operation in flight. The publisher's final check reads `paused`; an effect that passed it before the pause may finish. |
| `tick` | No launch, no task allocation, no budget charge; reminders are suppressed. The one tick row is the controller's resume of its own stop after a processing error, once the pipeline code changed. |

## Transitions

For each state, the verbs available from it. A verb leads from a state to one target only. *Same state* means the transition keeps phase and activity.

### `queued.idle`
{: #state-queued-idle }

| Verb | Trigger | To | Guard | Effects | Charges |
|:-----|:--------|:---|:------|:--------|:--------|
| `begin_planning` | tick | `planning.idle` | not paused | none | - |
| `withdraw_request` | observation | `closed.idle` | intake label removed; no task requested; no plan; no fork | sets `terminal_reason=withdrawn`; clears `paused`, `paused_at`, `paused_reason`, `paused_by`, `paused_at_commit` | - |
| `require_base_branch` | observation | `planning.waiting_human` | the upstream says that the base branch does not exist or was renamed; not paused; quiescent: no open operation and no pending publication. Records whether the branch does not exist or was renamed, and to which name. While the contribution waits, the upstream is read again only once an authorized resume is posted. Once the branch exists again, a resume continues; to continue on another branch, the contribution is parked first and then restarted on that branch. | sets `pending_human_action=base_branch_unavailable` | - |
| `exhaust_source_reads` | observation | `planning.waiting_human` | source_reads exhausted: reads of the upstream kept failing for the whole retry window, most of them for the base branch; not paused; quiescent: no open operation and no pending publication. Records how many failed reads were counted, since when, how many of them could not read the repository itself, and the last error. The upstream is still read on every tick, and once it can be read again the wait ends without a human (`resume_upstream_read`); a resume reads it again at once. | sets `pending_human_action=base_branch_unavailable`, `pending_human_action.counter=source_reads` | - |
| `require_upstream_access` | observation | `planning.waiting_human` | source_reads exhausted: reads of the upstream kept failing for the whole retry window, most of them for the repository itself; not paused; quiescent: no open operation and no pending publication. Taken once failed reads of the repository itself are the majority of the retry window (deleted, made private, or no longer readable with the token). Records the repository and the counted reads. The upstream is still read on every tick, and once it can be read again the wait ends without a human (`resume_upstream_read`); a resume reads it again at once. | sets `pending_human_action=upstream_unavailable`, `pending_human_action.counter=source_reads` | - |
| `require_renamed_upstream` | observation | `planning.waiting_human` | GitHub answers for the recorded upstream repository id under another name (renamed or transferred); not paused; quiescent: no open operation and no pending publication. | `park_contribution` (rule) | command (`/upstreaming park`) | `parked.idle` | a reason is given; any revision, current or stale; no open operation. Accepted while paused. | Task: clear; sets `parked_reason`, `previous_phase`; clears `pending_publication` | - |
| `record_source_unavailable` (rule) | observation | same state | the upstream repository or its base branch could not be read, and the upstream did not say that the branch is missing; source_reads remains; not paused; quiescent: no open operation and no pending publication. A failed read is charged only when it is the first of a run, or when it falls in a later spacing slot than the last charged read (slots of `retries.source_unavailable_minutes` divided by `retries.source_unavailable_reads`, counted from the first failed read, so that a tick a little early or late still counts); a failed read in the same slot writes nothing, so a burst of ticks adds no events, and a read after a long pause counts once. | `record_late_effect` (rule) | result | same state | the Result does not match the current generation, revision, and a requested task. Recorded in the events for audit. The Result is never folded, the publisher refuses it, and the state never changes. | none | - |

### `planning.agent_running`
{: #state-planning-agent_running }

| Verb | Trigger | To | Guard | Effects | Charges |
|:-----|:--------|:---|:------|:--------|:--------|
| `retry_dispatch` | tick | same state | a dispatcher run ended with the requested task absent or unclaimed; dispatch_recovery remains. Launches the dispatcher again for the same committed task request. The row records the dispatcher run it decided in `active_task.dispatched_run_id`, so each ended run is decided once. | sets `active_task.dispatched_run_id` | `dispatch_recovery` |
| `exhaust_recovery` | tick | `planning.waiting_human` | the recovery of the failure is exhausted: dispatch_recovery for a lost dispatch, task_recovery or task_total for a task graph terminal without a usable Result, publish_recovery for a failed publication; the last Claim of the task did not fail before its agent for a failure of the pipeline. The pending action names the failure, and `pending_human_action.counter` the budget it spent: `dispatch_failed` with `dispatch_recovery` for a lost dispatch, which also records the version of the pipeline code it failed at (`pending_human_action.pipeline_version`) and the budgets the allocation of the lost task charged (`pending_human_action.credit`); `task_failed` for a task graph terminal without a usable Result, with `task_total` when that budget is exhausted (also when `task_recovery` is exhausted too) and `task_recovery` otherwise. The resume starts that counter again; `task_recovery` starts again with the fresh task. | Task: clear; sets `pending_human_action=dispatch_failed|task_failed`, `pending_human_action.counter`, `pending_human_action.pipeline_version`, `pending_human_action.credit` | - |
| `allocate_task_retry` | tick | same state | the task graph is terminal without a usable Result; the last Claim of the task did not fail before its agent for a failure of the pipeline; task_recovery and task_total remain; upstream identity and base bound. A terminal task graph is never submitted again; a fresh graph is allocated. It carries the same feedback ids. | revision +1; Task: reallocate | `task_recovery`, `task_total` |
| `reallocate_after_pipeline_failure` | tick | same state | the task graph is terminal without a usable Result; the last Claim of the task failed before its agent for a failure of the pipeline; the pipeline code changed since that failure, a human launched the controller, or the backoff of one of its 3 free relaunches passed; upstream identity and base bound. A fresh graph is allocated for a task graph whose last Claim failed before its agent for a failure of the pipeline, once the pipeline code changed since the failure, a human launched the controller, or the backoff of one of its 3 free relaunches passed (counted on the task as `pipeline_free`, per version of the code). It charges nothing: the failure was not caused by the task, so `task_recovery`, `task_total` and the attempts counted so far are unchanged. Until then the record is held as it is: no row is taken and the failure is reported as an alert. It carries the same feedback ids. A Result held for a publish-only retry whose report records no review loop (a worker run of the earlier pipeline) takes it too: the held Result is dropped with the task. So does a Result that no independent review covers (the worker's loop records unavailable reviewers, or the agent's log shows fewer successful reviewer launches than the rounds it reports), at most 3 times before each charged retry (`active_task.review_free`). | revision +1; Task: reallocate; clears `pending_publication` | - |
| `reject_plan` | result | `planning.idle` | the Result has no plan, the plan is invalid, its decision is not develop, park, or close, or PyPI does not confirm a decision close; planning_attempts remains. Trusted validation rejects the Result; a new planning run is due. | revision +1; Task: clear | `planning_attempts` |
| `exhaust_planning_recovery` | result | `planning.waiting_human` | the Result has no usable plan; planning_attempts exhausted | Task: clear; sets `pending_human_action=planning_failed`, `pending_human_action.counter=planning_attempts` | - |
| `admit_development` | result | `provisioning.idle` | verified plan decision develop, or verified plan decision park and a recorded admission_override; the admitted scope names an admission class and 1 to 64 safe `scope_paths`, and a plan's own scope matches every path of its `path_coverage`; no refresh recorded, or the recorded fork or development PR no longer matches. The scope of the patch is checked here, before a fork exists: no patch task is requested before `confirm_provisioning`. `scope_coverage_complete` records whether the admitted scope matches every path of the plan's `path_coverage`: always true for a plan's own scope, and for an admission override whatever the human's paths cover. | revision +1; Task: clear; sets `plan_evidence_id`, `admission_class`, `scope_paths`, `scope_coverage_complete`; clears `refresh`, `admission_override` | - |
| `readmit_development` | result | `development.fix_needed` | verified plan decision develop, or verified plan decision park and a recorded admission_override; the admitted scope names an admission class and 1 to 64 safe `scope_paths`, and a plan's own scope matches every path of its `path_coverage`; refresh recorded; the recorded fork and development PR still match. A refreshed planning returns to the existing fork for repair. The scope is checked as for `admit_development`: a refreshed plan whose scope is incomplete takes `reject_plan`. | revision +1; Task: clear; sets `plan_evidence_id`, `admission_class`, `scope_paths`, `scope_coverage_complete`; clears `refresh`, `admission_override` | - |
| `park_planning` | result | `parked.idle` | verified plan decision park; no admission_override recorded | Task: clear; sets `parked_reason`, `previous_phase`; clears `pending_publication` | - |
| `close_planning` | result | `closed.idle` | verified plan decision close; PyPI serves riscv64 for the latest release of every distribution, and each PyPI project names the upstream repository: a riscv64 wheel, or pure-Python wheels only. A project that is not released on PyPI is never closed by its plan: it is parked with the evidence. A recorded `admission_override` is not applied against a decision close; the reply states so. | Task: clear; sets `terminal_reason`; clears `pending_publication`, `paused`, `paused_at`, `paused_reason`, `paused_by`, `paused_at_commit` | - |
| `park_contribution` (rule) | command (`/upstreaming park`) | `parked.idle` | a reason is given; any revision, current or stale; no open operation. A wait the upstream's own answer caused (a missing or renamed branch) still needs a resume. | revision +1; clears `pending_human_action`; starts again the counter named in `pending_human_action.counter` (one of `source_reads`) | - |
| `require_base_branch` | tick | same state | the wait was entered because GitHub named the recorded repository otherwise: its pending action names no counter; the upstream says that the base branch does not exist or was renamed; not paused; quiescent: no open operation and no pending publication. | `record_late_effect` (rule) | result | same state | the Result does not match the current generation, revision, and a requested task. Recorded in the events for audit. The Result is never folded, the publisher refuses it, and the state never changes. | none | - |

CI is a function of the tree: when the reviewed series has the tree of the candidate head (the approved series had no debug commit), the CI evidence of the candidate head is CI on the clean head. | sets `last_ci_evidence_id` | - |
| `rerun_interrupted_ci` | observation | same state | a required CI job on the exact head was cancelled or lost its runner; interrupted_reruns remains. The collector reruns the interrupted jobs on the exact head. It reruns for no other conclusion. The collector records a `ci_rerun` operation that the trusted workflow executes; a rerun that fails is requested again by this row within the budget. The bounded wait for CI on the clean head starts again, since CI was started again. | sets `clean_head_ci_since` | `interrupted_reruns` |
| `exhaust_interrupted_reruns` | observation | `handoff.waiting_human` | a required CI job on the exact head was cancelled or lost its runner; interrupted_reruns exhausted | sets `pending_human_action=ci_interrupted`, `pending_human_action.counter=interrupted_reruns` | - |
| `return_for_repair` | observation | `development.fix_needed` | a blocking CI failure on the clean head, or the observed `riscv64` head differs from the clean head. A blocking failure records the failing evidence of the clean head as `last_ci_evidence_id`, so the repair requested in `development.fix_needed` names the failing job and charges its cluster. A `riscv64` head that is not the clean head has no CI verdict: the recorded evidence of the candidate head is kept. | revision +1; sets `last_ci_evidence_id`; clears `clean_head_sha`, `clean_head_ci_since`, `submission_rewrite_id`, `handoff_request`, `pending_human_action` | - |
| `require_clean_head_ci` | observation | `handoff.waiting_human` | CI on the clean head is not complete, and either no run exists and its workflow cannot be dispatched, or 12 hours have passed since the wait began. The pending action names the missing CI on the clean head; a human runs it (or makes it runnable) and resumes, which observes CI on the clean head again. | sets `pending_human_action=clean_head_ci_missing` | - |
| `park_contribution` (rule) | command (`/upstreaming park`) | `parked.idle` | a reason is given; any revision, current or stale; no open operation. Ends the current generation; evidence is kept for audit. A Result held for publication is not published. Accepted while paused. | Task: clear; sets `parked_reason`, `previous_phase`; clears `pending_publication` | - |
| `record_late_effect` (rule) | result | same state | the Result does not match the current generation, revision, and a requested task. Recorded in the events for audit. The Result is never folded, the publisher refuses it, and the state never changes. | none | - |

### `handoff.waiting_human`
{: #state-handoff-waiting_human }

| Verb | Trigger | To | Guard | Effects | Charges |
|:-----|:--------|:---|:------|:--------|:--------|
| `rearm_dispatch` | tick | `handoff.review_due` | pending_human_action is dispatch_failed; the work-queue Policy was installed after the dispatch failed and the compiled policy preserves it, or the pipeline code changed since the dispatch failed; not paused; quiescent: no open operation and no pending publication. Re-arms a dispatch that failed, once its cause can have changed: the dispatcher reinstalled the compiled policy that the installed one refused, or the pipeline code changed since the failure (a resume once per version of the code, which the next failure records). The task the lost dispatch allocated is given back its budgets: `task_total` (and the repair counter of its failing CI job) as its allocation charged them (`pending_human_action.credit`), `task_total` alone for a wait that records none. The same transition as the resume a human would post, taken by the controller. | revision +1; clears `pending_human_action`; starts again the counter named in `pending_human_action.counter` (one of `dispatch_recovery`); gives back `task_total`, `repair_attempts_cluster` as the lost allocation charged them (`pending_human_action.credit`) | - |
| `resume_submission_review` | command (`/upstreaming resume`) | `handoff.review_due` | exact revision; pending_human_action is task_budget_exhausted, dispatch_failed, task_failed, base_branch_unavailable, or upstream_unavailable. A fresh rewrite task is requested; it reviews its own series in its run. When an exhausted budget caused the wait, the resume starts again the one counter named in `pending_human_action.counter`, and no other. The event records the actor, the counter, and its count at that point. | revision +1; clears `pending_human_action`; starts again the counter named in `pending_human_action.counter` (one of `task_total`, `dispatch_recovery`, `task_recovery`, `source_reads`) | - |
| `resume_upstream_branch` | command (`/upstreaming resume`) | `handoff.building_upstream_branch` | exact revision; pending_human_action is upstream_branch_failed or upstream_branch_blocked | revision +1; clears `pending_human_action`; starts again the counter named in `pending_human_action.counter` (one of `upstream_branch`) | - |
| `resume_ci` | command (`/upstreaming resume`) | `handoff.waiting_ci` | exact revision; pending_human_action is ci_interrupted or clean_head_ci_missing. CI on the clean head is observed again, and its bounded wait starts again. After `ci_interrupted` it also starts `interrupted_reruns` (`budget.reruns.interrupted`) again for the head; the first observation after it reruns the interrupted jobs through `rerun_interrupted_ci`, charging the restarted counter. `clean_head_ci_missing` names no counter, so nothing else starts again. | revision +1; sets `clean_head_ci_since`; clears `pending_human_action`; starts again the counter named in `pending_human_action.counter` (one of `interrupted_reruns`) | - |
| `resume_submission_preparation` | command (`/upstreaming resume`) | `handoff.preparing_submission` | exact revision; pending_human_action is submission_comment_failed | revision +1; clears `pending_human_action`; starts again the counter named in `pending_human_action.counter` (one of `submission_comment`) | - |
| `resume_upstream_read` | tick | `handoff.review_due` | pending_human_action is base_branch_unavailable or upstream_unavailable; the wait was entered because reads kept failing, or because GitHub named the recorded repository otherwise, not because the upstream said that the branch is missing; the upstream repository and its base branch are read again; not paused; quiescent: no open operation and no pending publication. Ends a wait that failed reads caused once a tick reads the upstream again, and the wait a renamed repository caused once a tick reads the repository under its recorded name and id again: the step that was due runs again, and the tracking issue states that the contribution continues. A wait the upstream's own answer caused (a missing or renamed branch) still needs a resume. | revision +1; clears `pending_human_action`; starts again the counter named in `pending_human_action.counter` (one of `source_reads`) | - |
| `require_base_branch` | tick | same state | the wait was entered because GitHub named the recorded repository otherwise: its pending action names no counter; the upstream says that the base branch does not exist or was renamed; not paused; quiescent: no open operation and no pending publication. Taken once the repository is read under its recorded name and id again and the upstream says that the base branch does not exist or was renamed: the wait stays, and its cause becomes the base branch, as `require_base_branch` records it from the state the step was due in. While the contribution waits, the upstream is read again only once an authorized resume is posted. Once the branch exists again, a resume continues; to continue on another branch, the contribution is parked first and then restarted on that branch. | sets `pending_human_action=base_branch_unavailable` | - |
| `park_contribution` (rule) | command (`/upstreaming park`) | `parked.idle` | a reason is given; any revision, current or stale; no open operation. Ends the current generation; evidence is kept for audit. A Result held for publication is not published. Accepted while paused. | Task: clear; sets `parked_reason`, `previous_phase`; clears `pending_publication` | - |
| `record_reminder` (rule) | tick | same state | at least `human_sla_business_days.reminder` business days since the request or the last reminder; not paused. Posts an append-only reminder of the pending human step. In `handoff.waiting_upstream_pr` the reminder text carries the package link and the exact head, and states when an observed PR does not match. Days are whole days from the exact time of the request or of the last reminder; a day counts when it ends on a weekday (UTC). A reminder that came due during a pause is posted after the resume, in the same tick. | sets `pending_human_action.reminded_at` | - |
| `record_late_effect` (rule) | result | same state | the Result does not match the current generation, revision, and a requested task. Recorded in the events for audit. The Result is never folded, the publisher refuses it, and the state never changes. | none | - |

### `upstream_review.fix_needed`
{: #state-upstream_review-fix_needed }

| Verb | Trigger | To | Guard | Effects | Charges |
|:-----|:--------|:---|:------|:--------|:--------|
| `request_upstream_revision` | tick | `upstream_review.agent_running` | the upstream PR head is the controlled fork ref; a failing CI job is recorded for the head; worker slot free; repair_attempts_cluster, no_progress, and task_total remain; not paused; no open operation; upstream identity and base bound. Charges `repair_attempts_cluster` for the failing CI job. The task request carries the pending feedback ids present at allocation (`active_task.feedback_evidence_ids`). | Task: allocate; sets `active_task.feedback_evidence_ids` | `repair_attempts_cluster`, `task_total` |
| `request_review_revision` | tick | `upstream_review.agent_running` | the upstream PR head is the controlled fork ref; no failing CI job is recorded for the head; worker slot free; no_progress and task_total remain; not paused; no open operation; upstream identity and base bound. A revision driven only by review feedback; it charges no `repair_attempts_cluster`. The task request carries the pending feedback ids present at allocation (`active_task.feedback_evidence_ids`). | Task: allocate; sets `active_task.feedback_evidence_ids` | `task_total` |
| `exhaust_repair_attempts` | tick | `upstream_review.waiting_human` | no_progress or task_total is exhausted, or repair_attempts_cluster is exhausted and a failing CI job is recorded for the head. `pending_human_action.counter` names the first exhausted counter in the order `no_progress`, `task_total`, `repair_attempts_cluster`, and the event lists every exhausted counter. The resume starts only the named counter again, so with several exhausted the next tick waits again on the next one. | sets `pending_human_action=repair_budget_exhausted`, `pending_human_action.counter` | - |
| `require_base_branch` | observation | `upstream_review.waiting_human` | the upstream says that the base branch does not exist or was renamed; not paused; quiescent: no open operation and no pending publication. Records whether the branch does not exist or was renamed, and to which name. While the contribution waits, the upstream is read again only once an authorized resume is posted. Once the branch exists again, a resume continues; to continue on another branch, the contribution is parked first and then restarted on that branch. | sets `pending_human_action=base_branch_unavailable` | - |
| `exhaust_source_reads` | observation | `upstream_review.waiting_human` | source_reads exhausted: reads of the upstream kept failing for the whole retry window, most of them for the base branch; not paused; quiescent: no open operation and no pending publication. Records how many failed reads were counted, since when, how many of them could not read the repository itself, and the last error. The upstream is still read on every tick, and once it can be read again the wait ends without a human (`resume_upstream_read`); a resume reads it again at once. | sets `pending_human_action=base_branch_unavailable`, `pending_human_action.counter=source_reads` | - |
| `require_upstream_access` | observation | `upstream_review.waiting_human` | source_reads exhausted: reads of the upstream kept failing for the whole retry window, most of them for the repository itself; not paused; quiescent: no open operation and no pending publication. Taken once failed reads of the repository itself are the majority of the retry window (deleted, made private, or no longer readable with the token). Records the repository and the counted reads. The upstream is still read on every tick, and once it can be read again the wait ends without a human (`resume_upstream_read`); a resume reads it again at once. | sets `pending_human_action=upstream_unavailable`, `pending_human_action.counter=source_reads` | - |
| `require_renamed_upstream` | observation | `upstream_review.waiting_human` | GitHub answers for the recorded upstream repository id under another name (renamed or transferred); not paused; quiescent: no open operation and no pending publication. Taken at once, with no counter: the answer cannot change by reading again. Records the repository and the name GitHub now gives it, and `upstream.repository_id` becomes the id GitHub answered for (the recorded one when it is bound; for a request not bound yet, the id of the renamed repository, so that no other repository later created under the recorded name is taken for it). The upstream is still read on every tick, and once GitHub answers for the same repository id under its recorded name again the wait ends without a human (`resume_upstream_read`); a resume while it is still named otherwise waits again at once. Once it is answered for under its recorded name but its base branch is missing, `require_base_branch` replaces the wait. A repository that moved is a new request: the contribution is parked, then abandoned. | sets `pending_human_action=upstream_unavailable`, `upstream.repository_id` | - |
| `follow_renamed_base` | observation | same state | the upstream renamed the base branch, the open upstream PR now targets the new name, and the new name's history contains the recorded base commit; not paused; quiescent: no open operation and no pending publication. `upstream.base_ref` and the recorded base of the upstream PR become the new name; `upstream.base_sha` is kept, since the renamed branch still contains it. The tracking issue states the rename. | sets `upstream.base_ref`, `upstream_pr.base_ref` | - |
| `record_source_unavailable` (rule) | observation | same state | the upstream repository or its base branch could not be read, and the upstream did not say that the branch is missing; source_reads remains; not paused; quiescent: no open operation and no pending publication. A network error, a server error, a rate limit, or a repository that cannot be read: the contribution stays, and a later tick reads the upstream again. A failed read is charged only when it is the first of a run, or when it falls in a later spacing slot than the last charged read (slots of `retries.source_unavailable_minutes` divided by `retries.source_unavailable_reads`, counted from the first failed read, so that a tick a little early or late still counts); a failed read in the same slot writes nothing, so a burst of ticks adds no events, and a read after a long pause counts once. A tick that reads the upstream starts `source_reads` again. | none | `source_reads` |
| `record_late_effect` (rule) | result | same state | the Result does not match the current generation, revision, and a requested task. Recorded in the events for audit. The Result is never folded, the publisher refuses it, and the state never changes. | none | - |

### `upstream_review.agent_running`
{: #state-upstream_review-agent_running }

| Verb | Trigger | To | Guard | Effects | Charges |
|:-----|:--------|:---|:------|:--------|:--------|
| `record_revision_publish_success` | result | `upstream_review.waiting_ci` | the revision is published to the upstream PR head. The published revision answers exactly the feedback its task carried. `upstream_pr.head_sha` records the head the publisher read back on `riscv64` after its push. A publication whose push was not read back (`uncertain`) does not take this row: it is a failed publication (`schedule_publish_retry`), and the publish-only retry reads back the head a lost push left without pushing again. The report of the task is stored as `worker_report` evidence. | revision +1; Task: clear; sets `proposal_artifact`, `publication_operation_id`, `upstream_pr.head_sha`; clears `carried pending_feedback_evidence_ids`, `pending_publication`, `budget.no_progress_streak` | - |
| `reject_patch_proposal` | result | `upstream_review.fix_needed` | the proposal is rejected for the current revision, or the worker reports it is blocked; no_progress remains. The pending feedback is kept. The worker's report is discarded, unless this is a publish-only retry rejected as stale behind the operation of an earlier attempt: that push landed or may have, so the report is stored with the commit it proposed. | revision +1; Task: clear; clears `pending_publication` | `no_progress` |
| `require_reviewer_answer` | result | `upstream_review.waiting_human` | the worker reports that no change is needed. The worker found that no change is needed: a human answers the reviewer, or, when the task answered an upstream CI failure, judges that failure (the pipeline never reruns upstream CI) and resumes. The failure stays recorded, so the resume requests no revision for it, and a rerun that fails again is recorded anew. The pipeline posts nothing on the upstream PR. The report of the task is stored as `worker_report` evidence. | Task: clear; sets `pending_human_action=answer_reviewer`; clears `pending_publication` | - |
| `schedule_publish_retry` | result | same state | publication failed with an infrastructure error; publish_recovery remains. The same verified Result is published again; no new task is requested. The pending publication carries the feedback ids of its task. A publication whose push was not read back (`uncertain`) is such a failure; the retry reads the branch first and never pushes over a push that landed. Its push may have landed, so the report of an `uncertain` Result is stored as `worker_report` evidence with the commit it proposed, whatever ends the hold. | Task: clear; sets `pending_publication` | `publish_recovery` |
| `retry_dispatch` | tick | same state | a dispatcher run ended with the requested task absent or unclaimed; dispatch_recovery remains. Launches the dispatcher again for the same committed task request. The row records the dispatcher run it decided in `active_task.dispatched_run_id`, so each ended run is decided once. | sets `active_task.dispatched_run_id` | `dispatch_recovery` |
| `exhaust_recovery` | tick | `upstream_review.waiting_human` | the recovery of the failure is exhausted: dispatch_recovery for a lost dispatch, task_recovery or task_total for a task graph terminal without a usable Result, publish_recovery for a failed publication; the last Claim of the task did not fail before its agent for a failure of the pipeline. The pending action names the failure, and `pending_human_action.counter` the budget it spent: `dispatch_failed` with `dispatch_recovery` for a lost dispatch, which also records the version of the pipeline code it failed at (`pending_human_action.pipeline_version`) and the budgets the allocation of the lost task charged (`pending_human_action.credit`); `task_failed` for a task graph terminal without a usable Result, with `task_total` when that budget is exhausted (also when `task_recovery` is exhausted too) and `task_recovery` otherwise; `publication_infrastructure_failure` with `publish_recovery` for a failed publication, which keeps the held Result (`pending_publication.exhausted`). The resume starts that counter again; `task_recovery` starts again with the fresh task. | Task: clear; sets `pending_human_action=dispatch_failed|task_failed|publication_infrastructure_failure`, `pending_human_action.counter`, `pending_human_action.pipeline_version`, `pending_human_action.credit`, `pending_publication.exhausted` | - |
| `allocate_task_retry` | tick | same state | the task graph is terminal without a usable Result; the last Claim of the task did not fail before its agent for a failure of the pipeline; task_recovery and task_total remain; upstream identity and base bound. A terminal task graph is never submitted again; a fresh graph is allocated. It carries the same feedback ids. | revision +1; Task: reallocate | `task_recovery`, `task_total` |
| `reallocate_after_pipeline_failure` | tick | same state | the task graph is terminal without a usable Result; the last Claim of the task failed before its agent for a failure of the pipeline; the pipeline code changed since that failure, a human launched the controller, or the backoff of one of its 3 free relaunches passed; upstream identity and base bound. A fresh graph is allocated for a task graph whose last Claim failed before its agent for a failure of the pipeline, once the pipeline code changed since the failure, a human launched the controller, or the backoff of one of its 3 free relaunches passed (counted on the task as `pipeline_free`, per version of the code). It charges nothing: the failure was not caused by the task, so `task_recovery`, `task_total` and the attempts counted so far are unchanged. Until then the record is held as it is: no row is taken and the failure is reported as an alert. It carries the same feedback ids. A Result held for a publish-only retry whose report records no review loop (a worker run of the earlier pipeline) takes it too: the held Result is dropped with the task. So does a Result that no independent review covers (the worker's loop records unavailable reviewers, or the agent's log shows fewer successful reviewer launches than the rounds it reports), at most 3 times before each charged retry (`active_task.review_free`). | revision +1; Task: reallocate; clears `pending_publication` | - |
| `record_late_effect` (rule) | result | same state | the Result does not match the current generation, revision, and a requested task. Recorded in the events for audit. The Result is never folded, the publisher refuses it, and the state never changes. | none | - |

### `upstream_review.waiting_human`
{: #state-upstream_review-waiting_human }

| Verb | Trigger | To | Guard | Effects | Charges |
|:-----|:--------|:---|:------|:--------|:--------|
| `resume_upstream_review` | command (`/upstreaming resume`) | `upstream_review.waiting_ci` | exact revision; pending_human_action is pr_closed_unmerged, answer_reviewer, or upstream_head_changed; for pr_closed_unmerged, the upstream PR is observed open again or merged. No revision task is requested. The pending feedback is cleared: after `answer_reviewer` a human answered it, and this is the one resume that clears feedback; the other two pending actions are entered from `upstream_review.waiting_ci`, which holds none. A PR merged since it was closed is followed: the observation of `upstream_review.waiting_ci` takes `record_merge`. | revision +1; clears `pending_human_action`, `pending_feedback_evidence_ids` | - |
| `rearm_dispatch` | tick | `upstream_review.fix_needed` | pending_human_action is dispatch_failed; the work-queue Policy was installed after the dispatch failed and the compiled policy preserves it, or the pipeline code changed since the dispatch failed; not paused; quiescent: no open operation and no pending publication. Re-arms a dispatch that failed, once its cause can have changed: the dispatcher reinstalled the compiled policy that the installed one refused, or the pipeline code changed since the failure (a resume once per version of the code, which the next failure records). The task the lost dispatch allocated is given back its budgets: `task_total` (and the repair counter of its failing CI job) as its allocation charged them (`pending_human_action.credit`), `task_total` alone for a wait that records none. The same transition as the resume a human would post, taken by the controller. | revision +1; clears `pending_human_action`; starts again the counter named in `pending_human_action.counter` (one of `dispatch_recovery`); gives back `task_total`, `repair_attempts_cluster` as the lost allocation charged them (`pending_human_action.credit`) | - |
| `resume_upstream_revision` | command (`/upstreaming resume`) | `upstream_review.fix_needed` | exact revision; pending_human_action is dispatch_failed, task_failed, publication_infrastructure_failure, repair_budget_exhausted, base_branch_unavailable, or upstream_unavailable. Only when a revision task failed: dispatch, a task, publication, or a budget. The pending feedback is kept. When an exhausted budget caused the wait, the resume starts again the one counter named in `pending_human_action.counter`, and no other. The event records the actor, the counter, and its count at that point. | revision +1; clears `pending_human_action`, `pending_publication`; starts again the counter named in `pending_human_action.counter` (one of `repair_attempts_cluster`, `no_progress`, `task_total`, `dispatch_recovery`, `task_recovery`, `publish_recovery`, `source_reads`) | - |
| `resume_upstream_read` | tick | `upstream_review.fix_needed` | pending_human_action is base_branch_unavailable or upstream_unavailable; the wait was entered because reads kept failing, or because GitHub named the recorded repository otherwise, not because the upstream said that the branch is missing; the upstream repository and its base branch are read again; not paused; quiescent: no open operation and no pending publication. Ends a wait that failed reads caused once a tick reads the upstream again, and the wait a renamed repository caused once a tick reads the repository under its recorded name and id again: the step that was due runs again, and the tracking issue states that the contribution continues. A wait the upstream's own answer caused (a missing or renamed branch) still needs a resume. | revision +1; clears `pending_human_action`; starts again the counter named in `pending_human_action.counter` (one of `source_reads`) | - |
| `require_base_branch` | tick | same state | the wait was entered because GitHub named the recorded repository otherwise: its pending action names no counter; the upstream says that the base branch does not exist or was renamed; not paused; quiescent: no open operation and no pending publication. Taken once the repository is read under its recorded name and id again and the upstream says that the base branch does not exist or was renamed: the wait stays, and its cause becomes the base branch, as `require_base_branch` records it from the state the step was due in. While the contribution waits, the upstream is read again only once an authorized resume is posted. Once the branch exists again, a resume continues; to continue on another branch, the contribution is parked first and then restarted on that branch. | sets `pending_human_action=base_branch_unavailable` | - |
| `resume_renamed_base` | observation | `upstream_review.fix_needed` | pending_human_action is base_branch_unavailable; the upstream renamed the base branch, the open upstream PR now targets the new name, and the new name's history contains the recorded base commit; not paused; quiescent: no open operation and no pending publication. The wait a renamed base branch caused ends without a human: the record follows the rename as `follow_renamed_base` does, and the revision task that was due is due again. The tracking issue states the rename. | revision +1; sets `upstream.base_ref`, `upstream_pr.base_ref`; clears `pending_human_action`; starts again the counter named in `pending_human_action.counter` (one of `source_reads`) | - |
| `park_contribution` (rule) | command (`/upstreaming park`) | `parked.idle` | a reason is given; any revision, current or stale; no open operation. Ends the current generation; evidence is kept for audit. A Result held for publication is not published. Accepted while paused. | Task: clear; sets `parked_reason`, `previous_phase`; clears `pending_publication` | - |
| `record_reminder` (rule) | tick | same state | at least `human_sla_business_days.reminder` business days since the request or the last reminder; not paused. Posts an append-only reminder of the pending human step. In `handoff.waiting_upstream_pr` the reminder text carries the package link and the exact head, and states when an observed PR does not match. Days are whole days from the exact time of the request or of the last reminder; a day counts when it ends on a weekday (UTC). A reminder that came due during a pause is posted after the resume, in the same tick. | sets `pending_human_action.reminded_at` | - |
| `record_late_effect` (rule) | result | same state | the Result does not match the current generation, revision, and a requested task. Recorded in the events for audit. The Result is never folded, the publisher refuses it, and the state never changes. | none | - |
